newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire arrests dozens of army looters.
newsitem.headline: Zaire arrests dozens of army looters.

text.p: Zaire's army, cracking down on discipline after launching a counter-offensive against rebels in the east, has arrested scores of soldiers on charges of looting and desertion, a defence ministry official said.

The soldiers, who fled the battlefront at the end of last year and are accused of terrorising civilians in Upper Zaire province, were disarmed by military intelligence units and could face the death penalty if convicted, he added.

The official said a group of 150, mostly soldiers but including a handful of civilians, had been flown to the capital Kinshasa from the riverside town of Bumba in President Mobutu Sese Seko's home province of Equateur.
"They were disarmed at Bumba by the SARM (Military Action and Intelligence Services) on Tuesday and put in an airplane bound for Kinshasa," he added.
The official said the soldiers were accused of terrorising Upper Zaire province for over a month, looting, pillaging and killing civilians after fleeing the rebels.
They were being held in a military prison in Kinshasa and would be tried by a special tribunal.
A military tribunal in the eastern town of Kisangani condemned to death 14 soldiers, including four senior officers, a week ago for cowardice and desertion.
